page: Amazon Web Services m8idb.2xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose virtual instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a dedicated 64-bit x86 Intel processor operating at a clock frequency of 3.9 GHz. The compute configuration delivers 8 vCPUs distributed across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, paired with 32 GB of system memory. This maintains a standard general-purpose memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 4 GB per virtual core, providing balanced execution capacity for balanced enterprise compute requirements.

A key characteristic of the m8idb instance class is integrated high-speed storage. The m8idb.2xlarge is equipped with 474 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage. This hardware layer delivers low latency and high read/write throughput directly to the guest operating system, bypassing network-attached block storage overhead. Network connectivity features an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile, facilitating stable transfer rates for distributed operations. The configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and operates without discrete GPU acceleration hardware.

From a cost efficiency and architectural perspective, bundling 474 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage within a balanced 8-vCPU instance reduces the necessity for dedicated external low-latency volumes, lowering cumulative deployment footprint. However, because local instance store volumes are ephemeral, persistent storage architectures require external synchronization or continuous replication strategies. The instance profile is well structured for relational databases with read replicas, caching tiers, continuous integration build nodes, containerized microservices, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines requiring rapid scratch space.
